assignments.brief_reason: Moderation depended on harsh/profane tone rather than threats/toxicity or free-speech exceptions.
Removal was driven by lack of conversational value/context, not primarily threats/toxicity or violence exceptions.
“Professionalism standard” influenced judgments as a pair, but no clear linkage to consistent standards across viewpoints or threat/toxicity thresholds.
Threatening/vicious tone and heavy cussing functioned as key removal signals for toxicity.
Explicit claim of applying the same moderation standard to both posts independent of political position, using tone/target rules to reduce bias.
Used a profanity/cursing threshold to reject both; fits removing for toxic language though framed as a blunt rule.
Reject/allow depended on angry curse words and name-calling signals indicating toxicity.
Personal/side attacks (vs info) drove rejection; aligns more with removing toxic attacks than factual/violence exceptions.
Free-speech absolutism with removals mainly when posts attack or aren’t thoughtful; no explicit violence/incitement exception.
Removal was attributed to anti-censorship and only bad grammar/confusing syntax or insults, not clearly threat/toxicity or violence exception.
Generally tolerated non-nice speech but drew a line at vulgarity for vulgarity’s sake, indicating a toxic-language boundary.
Pair-comparison used perspective-taking to judge plausibility/falsehood harm, not the codebook themes’ moderation-consistency or threat-only exceptions.
Distinguished “true viewpoint” vs “nonsense” across both sides; not primarily threat/toxicity, free-speech with violence exceptions, or viewpoint-pair consistency.
Keep speech unless explicitly inciting violence or very profane, matching violence/threat exception logic.
Removal was driven by factual inaccuracy/misinformation verification rather than threat/toxicity or free-speech violence exceptions.
Critiqued the moderation approach based on extreme tradeoffs and misinformation; no primary mapping to the threat/toxicity or consistency themes.
Would allow if respectful but remove for pointless insulting personal attacks; most consistent with removing toxic/insulting content.
Removed when posts seemed like complete rumors; this is tone/quality-based rather than clearly threats/violence, but aligns closest with toxicity-style rejection.
Emphasized argument construction/validity and debate worthiness rather than moderation standard consistency or threat/toxicity exceptions.
Decisions were affected by the participant’s political affiliation and wording; not described as pair-consistency or threat/toxicity-based removal.
